newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher while pork belly futures were called steady to 0.300 cent per lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Hot, humid weather was expected to lend support to lean hog futures as such weather will support cash hog prices in much of the western Corn Belt. Higher pork cutout values were also seen supportive as well as indications the Cold Storage report was a little constructive despite larger-than-year ago ham and loin supplies. Total pork holdings were less than some had expected, analysts said.
However, trade was expected to remain cautious ahead of Friday's quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs report, they said.

Early analyst estimates on the report put all hogs on U.S. farms as of June 1 at 102 to 104 percent of last year. Kept for breeding numbers ranged from 103 to 106 percent and kept for marketing 101 to 105 percent.
The latest CME lean hog index jumped $1.10 to $81.50 per cwt.

Pork belly futures were expected to show early support on the Cold Storage report which showed May 31 belly stocks at the second lowest level on record. A firmer tone to the cash belly market and expected reduced hog slaughter due to heat-restricted hog movement was also supportive, they said.
The storage report showed frozen pork belly stocks at 55.713 million lbs, only slightly above the record low for a May 31 supply of 54.98 million lbs.
